Deprecated typedef alias for C99 uint8_t (8-bit unsigned integer). Prefer using uint8_t.
Deprecated typedef alias for C99 int16_t (16-bit signed integer). Prefer using int16_t.
Deprecated typedef alias for C99 uint16_t (16-bit unsigned integer). Prefer using uint16_t.
Deprecated typedef alias for C99 int32_t (32-bit signed integer). Prefer using int32_t.
Deprecated typedef alias for C99 uint32_t (32-bit unsigned integer). Prefer using uint32_t.
Deprecated typedef alias for C99 int64_t (64-bit signed integer). Prefer using int64_t.

Alias used to document passing of a uint16 value through varargs (promoted to int). Intended for APIs using va_list. It is effectively an int typedef.
Struct for the minimal TIFF header fields shared by ClassicTIFF and BigTIFF: byte-order magic and version. Typically read from the start of a TIFF file.
Classic TIFF (32-bit) header including the 32-bit offset to the first IFD (directory).

objects.definition:
typedef enum
{
    TIFF_NOTYPE = 0,     /* placeholder */
    TIFF_BYTE = 1,       /* 8-bit unsigned integer */
    TIFF_ASCII = 2,      /* 8-bit bytes w/ last byte null */
    TIFF_SHORT = 3,      /* 16-bit unsigned integer */
    TIFF_LONG = 4,       /* 32-bit unsigned integer */
    TIFF_RATIONAL = 5,   /* 64-bit unsigned fraction */
    TIFF_SBYTE = 6,      /* !8-bit signed integer */
    TIFF_UNDEFINED = 7,  /* !8-bit untyped data */
    TIFF_SSHORT = 8,     /* !16-bit signed integer */
    TIFF_SLONG = 9,      /* !32-bit signed integer */
    TIFF_SRATIONAL = 10, /* !64-bit signed fraction */
    TIFF_FLOAT = 11,     /* !32-bit IEEE floating point */
    TIFF_DOUBLE = 12,    /* !64-bit IEEE floating point */
    TIFF_IFD = 13,       /* %32-bit unsigned integer (offset) */
    TIFF_LONG8 = 16,     /* BigTIFF 64-bit unsigned integer */
    TIFF_SLONG8 = 17,    /* BigTIFF 64-bit signed integer */
    TIFF_IFD8 = 18       /* BigTIFF 64-bit unsigned integer (offset) */
} TIFFDataType;
objects.description: Enumeration of TIFF field data types used in tag definitions and I/O logic, including ClassicTIFF and BigTIFF-specific types.

No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only contains preprocessor macros with version information for libtiff. Consequently, there are no custom data types to document.
Opaque handle to a TIFF image/file context. Defined as an incomplete struct to hide internal fields from clients; all interaction is via the public API functions in this header.
Signed machine-size integer type used by the API for buffer sizes and counts. Signed to allow -1 error returns. tsize_t is deprecated alias kept for backward compatibility.
Unsigned 64-bit type for file offsets within TIFF/BigTIFF files. Distinct from off_t to ensure consistent unsigned semantics across platforms.
Unsigned 32-bit directory index type used to address directories within a TIFF file.
Deprecated alias for a directory tag identifier. Replaced by uint32_t in modern APIs.
Deprecated sample index type within a pixel. Retained for source compatibility.

objects.definition:
typedef uint32_t tstrile_t; /* strip or tile number */
typedef tstrile_t tstrip_t; /* strip number */
typedef tstrile_t ttile_t;  /* tile number */
objects.description: Unsigned 32-bit index for a strip-or-tile ("strile"). tstrip_t and ttile_t are deprecated aliases for strip and tile indices, respectively.
Generic pointer to image data buffers passed to/returned from I/O routines. Deprecated in favor of explicit void* usage.

objects.description: Opaque client data/file handle type used by client I/O callbacks. On Win32 it maps to a Windows HANDLE; otherwise it is a void* provided by the client.
8-bit component value used by RGBA utilities for color channels and LUTs.
Holds colorimetric and device characteristics for a display: XYZ-to-luminance matrix, reference white output, black residual light, and per-channel gamma, used by color conversion routines.
State and lookup tables for fast YCbCr to RGB conversion. Must be allocated as a single contiguous buffer large enough to hold the struct and LUTs as noted in the comment.
Conversion context for CIE L*a*b* to RGB, including reference white, device display parameters, and precomputed tables for the Y components.

State for reading and converting image data to 8-bit packed ABGR rasters via TIFFReadRGBAImage[...] and related helpers, including dimensions, orientation, colormap pointers, and function pointers for get/put routines and color conversion contexts.
Function pointer type for codec initialization routines. Returns nonzero on success.
Describes a compression codec: human-readable name, scheme identifier, and its initialization function. Instances are returned/registered via codec management APIs.
Simple unsigned rational number with numerator/denominator storage, typically for tag values that are rational numbers.
Opaque descriptor of a TIFF tag/field definition used by custom tag handling APIs. Actual structure is private to the library.
Opaque container describing an array of TIFFField definitions for custom directory reading/creation.
Function pointer type for setting a tag value through a varargs interface.
Function pointer type for getting a tag value through a varargs interface.
Function pointer type to print directory/tag information for a TIFF to a FILE*.
Vtable of client-overridable methods for setting/getting/printing tags on a TIFF handle.
Opaque set of options controlling behavior of TIFFOpen* functions (limits, handlers, warnings). Allocated/freed via dedicated APIs.

objects.definition:
typedef struct
{
    uint32_t field_tag;             /* field's tag */
    short field_readcount;          /* read count/TIFF_VARIABLE/TIFF_SPP */
    short field_writecount;         /* write count/TIFF_VARIABLE */
    TIFFDataType field_type;        /* type of associated data */
    unsigned short field_bit;       /* bit in fieldsset bit vector */
    unsigned char field_oktochange; /* if true, can change while writing */
    unsigned char field_passcount;  /* if true, pass dir count on set */
    char *field_name;               /* ASCII name */
} TIFFFieldInfo;
objects.description: Obsoleted public structure describing a tag/field’s metadata for legacy custom tag extensions. Use newer TIFFField/TIFFFieldArray APIs instead.
Opaque TIFF handle type referenced from included libtiff headers. This header does not define it; it only declares stream-based open functions that return this pointer.
C++ output stream class from the standard library, referenced as a parameter type. Not defined in this header.
C++ input stream class from the standard library, referenced as a parameter type. Not defined in this header.

functions.name: TIFFGetVersion
functions.description: Returns a static string describing the libtiff version.
requirements: No arguments.
Return value is a const pointer to a static, null-terminated string; do not free.

functions.name: TIFFFindCODEC
functions.description: Finds a registered codec by compression scheme value.
requirements: Input compression scheme must be a valid TIFF compression value.
Returns NULL if not found; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: TIFFRegisterCODEC
functions.description: Registers a codec identified by compression scheme, name, and init function.
requirements: Name must be a valid null-terminated string or non-NULL.
Init function must be a valid function pointer implementing TIFFInitMethod.
Compression scheme should not collide with an existing one unless overriding is intended.

functions.name: TIFFUnRegisterCODEC
functions.description: Unregisters a previously registered codec.
requirements: Argument must be a pointer previously returned by TIFFRegisterCODEC or part of configured codecs.
Safe to pass NULL only if library tolerates it (unknown).

functions.name: TIFFIsCODECConfigured
functions.description: Checks whether a codec for the specified compression scheme is configured (available).
requirements: Input must be a compression scheme value.
Returns nonzero if configured, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: TIFFGetConfiguredCODECs
functions.description: Returns an array/list of configured codecs.
requirements: Return format/termination is library-defined (unknown).
Returned memory ownership and lifetime are library-defined (unknown); do not modify unless documented.

functions.name: _TIFFmalloc
functions.description: Allocates s bytes using libtiff’s allocator.
requirements: s must be >= 0 and typically > 0 to allocate memory.
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check and free with _TIFFfree.

functions.name: _TIFFcalloc
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array of nmemb elements of siz bytes each.
requirements: nmemb and siz must be >= 0 and their product must not overflow tmsize_t.
Returns NULL on failure; free with _TIFFfree.

functions.name: _TIFFrealloc
functions.description: Changes the size of the memory block pointed to by p to s bytes using libtiff’s allocator.
requirements: p may be NULL to behave like _TIFFmalloc.
s must be >= 0.
Returns NULL on failure; original block may be unchanged; free successful allocations with _TIFFfree.

functions.name: _TIFFfree
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by _TIFFmalloc/_TIFFcalloc/_TIFFrealloc.
requirements: p must be a pointer previously returned by libtiff allocation functions or NULL.
Do not double-free.

functions.name: _TIFFmemset
functions.description: Sets c bytes at p to byte value v (memset wrapper using tmsize_t).
requirements: p must point to a buffer of at least c bytes.
c must be >= 0.

functions.name: _TIFFmemcpy
functions.description: Copies c bytes from s to d (memcpy wrapper using tmsize_t).
requirements: d and s must point to valid, non-overlapping buffers of at least c bytes.
c must be >= 0.

functions.name: _TIFFmemcmp
functions.signature: int _TIFFmemcmp(const void *p1, const void *p2, tmsize_t c);
functions.description: Compares c bytes at p1 and p2 (memcmp wrapper using tmsize_t).
requirements: p1 and p2 must point to valid buffers of at least c bytes.
c must be >= 0.

functions.name: TIFFGetTagListCount
functions.description: Returns the number of tags in the list for the given TIFF object.
requirements: tif must be a valid TIFF* opened by TIFFOpen/TIFFClientOpen et al.

functions.name: TIFFGetTagListEntry
functions.description: Returns the tag identifier at the given index in the tag list.
requirements: tif must be valid.
tag_index must be in [0, TIFFGetTagListCount(tif)-1].

functions.name: TIFFFindField
functions.description: Finds a field (tag definition) by tag and data type.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Data type may be TIFF_ANY to ignore type matching.
Returns NULL if not found; caller must handle NULL.

functions.name: TIFFFieldWithTag
functions.description: Gets the field definition for a tag.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Returns NULL if the tag is unknown.

functions.name: TIFFFieldWithName
functions.description: Gets the field definition by tag name.
requirements: tif must be valid.
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated string.
Returns NULL if not found.

functions.name: TIFFFieldTag
functions.description: Returns the numeric tag value from a TIFFField descriptor.
requirements: Input pointer must be a valid TIFFField*.

functions.name: TIFFFieldName
functions.description: Returns the name string of a TIFFField.
requirements: Input TIFFField* must be valid.
Return is a const pointer; do not free.

functions.name: TIFFFieldDataType
functions.description: Returns the declared data type of a TIFFField.
requirements: Input TIFFField* must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFFieldPassCount
functions.description: Indicates if the field expects the count to be passed (varargs API detail).
requirements: Input TIFFField* must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFFieldReadCount
functions.description: Returns the expected read count for the field, or special markers (e.g., TIFF_VARIABLE/TIFF_SPP).
requirements: Input TIFFField* must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFFieldWriteCount
functions.description: Returns the expected write count for the field, or special markers.
requirements: Input TIFFField* must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFFieldSetGetSize
functions.description: Returns the internal storage size of TIFFSet/Get field type in bytes.
requirements: Input TIFFField* must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFFieldSetGetCountSize
functions.description: Returns the size of the count parameter for the field: 0 (none), 2 (uint16_t), or 4 (uint32_t).
requirements: Input TIFFField* must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFFieldIsAnonymous
functions.description: Checks whether the field is an anonymous (undocumented) tag.
requirements: Input TIFFField* must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFAccessTagMethods
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the tag methods (vset/vget/printdir) for a TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Returned pointer refers to internal structures; modify only as intended by API.

functions.name: TIFFGetClientInfo
functions.description: Retrieves client info value associated with a key string on a TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.
key must be a null-terminated string.

functions.name: TIFFSetClientInfo
functions.description: Associates a user pointer with a key string on a TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.
key must be a null-terminated string.
Value pointer may be NULL to clear (behavior of NULL is library-defined).

functions.name: TIFFCleanup
functions.description: Cleans up a TIFF handle’s internal resources without closing the underlying file descriptor.
requirements: tif must be a valid TIFF*.
Do not use tif for further I/O after cleanup unless reinitialized (library-defined).

functions.name: TIFFClose
functions.description: Closes the TIFF handle and releases associated resources.
requirements: tif must be a valid TIFF* opened by TIFFOpen/TIFFClientOpen/etc.
After call, tif must not be used.

functions.name: TIFFFlush
functions.description: Flushes pending data and directory to the file as appropriate.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: TIFFFlushData
functions.description: Flushes only pending image data to the file.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: TIFFGetField
functions.description: Retrieves the value(s) of a tag via varargs.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Provide addresses of appropriate types per tag definition for output parameters.
Returns 1 if tag is set, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: TIFFVGetField
functions.signature: int TIFFVGetField(TIFF *tif, uint32_t tag, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of TIFFGetField.
requirements: tif must be valid.
ap must be initialized to receive appropriate pointer arguments.
Returns 1 if tag is set, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: TIFFGetFieldDefaulted
functions.description: Like TIFFGetField but returns default values if the tag is not explicitly set.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Provide addresses of appropriate types per tag definition.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted
functions.signature: int TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted(TIFF *tif, uint32_t tag, va_list ap);
functions.description: va_list variant of TIFFGetFieldDefaulted.
requirements: tif must be valid.
ap must be properly initialized.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: TIFFReadDirectory
functions.description: Reads the next directory (IFD) in the TIFF file into the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid and associated with an open file positioned at or before a directory.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure or end.

functions.name: TIFFReadCustomDirectory
functions.signature: int TIFFReadCustomDirectory(TIFF *tif, toff_t diroff, const TIFFFieldArray *infoarray);
functions.description: Reads a directory at explicit offset using a custom field array definition.
requirements: tif must be valid.
diroff must reference a valid directory offset in the file.
infoarray must describe the custom tags used in that directory.

functions.name: TIFFReadEXIFDirectory
functions.description: Reads an EXIF IFD located at diroff.
requirements: tif must be valid.
diroff must be a valid offset to an EXIF directory.

functions.name: TIFFReadGPSDirectory
functions.description: Reads a GPS IFD located at diroff.
requirements: tif must be valid.
diroff must be a valid offset to a GPS directory.

functions.name: TIFFScanlineSize64
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a scanline for the current image, as 64-bit.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Image must have valid geometry tags set.

functions.name: TIFFScanlineSize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a scanline for the current image, tmsize_t-sized.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFRasterScanlineSize64
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a scanline in the RGBA raster format, 64-bit.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFRasterScanlineSize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a scanline in the RGBA raster format.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFStripSize64
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a strip for the current image, 64-bit.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Image must be organized in strips.

functions.name: TIFFStripSize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a strip for the current image.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFRawStripSize64
functions.description: Returns the stored (raw) byte count of a specific strip, 64-bit.
requirements: tif must be valid.
strip must be in [0, TIFFNumberOfStrips(tif)-1].

functions.name: TIFFRawStripSize
functions.description: Returns the stored (raw) byte count of a specific strip.
requirements: tif must be valid.
strip index must be in range.

functions.name: TIFFVStripSize64
functions.description: Returns the size of a strip with nrows rows, 64-bit.
requirements: tif must be valid.
nrows must be > 0 and within image height.

functions.name: TIFFVStripSize
functions.description: Returns the size of a strip with nrows rows.
requirements: tif must be valid.
nrows must be > 0 and within image height.

functions.name: TIFFTileRowSize64
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a row within a tile, 64-bit.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Image must be organized in tiles.

functions.name: TIFFTileRowSize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a row within a tile.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFTileSize64
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of a tile, 64-bit.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Image must be tiled.

functions.name: TIFFTileSize
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of a tile.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFVTileSize64
functions.description: Returns the size of a tile with nrows rows, 64-bit.
requirements: tif must be valid.
nrows must be > 0 and within tile height.

functions.name: TIFFVTileSize
functions.description: Returns the size of a tile with nrows rows.
requirements: tif must be valid.
nrows must be > 0 and within tile height.

functions.name: TIFFDefaultStripSize
functions.description: Computes a reasonable default strip size given a requested size (hint).
requirements: tif must be valid.
request may be 0 for library default.

functions.name: TIFFDefaultTileSize
functions.description: Computes default tile width and height for an image.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Output pointers for width and height must be non-NULL.

functions.name: TIFFFileno
functions.description: Returns the underlying file descriptor (if available) for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.
May return -1 if not applicable.

functions.name: TIFFSetFileno
functions.description: Sets the underlying file descriptor for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Descriptor must refer to an open file with appropriate access.

functions.name: TIFFClientdata
functions.description: Returns the client data handle associated with the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFSetClientdata
functions.description: Sets the client data handle for the TIFF handle and returns previous value.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFGetMode
functions.description: Returns the open mode flags of the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFSetMode
functions.description: Sets the open mode flags on the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Mode value must be a valid combination understood by libtiff.

functions.name: TIFFIsTiled
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the image is organized in tiles.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFIsByteSwapped
functions.description: Returns nonzero if byte-swapping is required for data (file endianness differs from host).
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFIsUpSampled
functions.description: Returns nonzero if up-sampling is enabled for some data paths.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFIsMSB2LSB
functions.description: Returns nonzero if bits are ordered most-significant to least-significant within bytes.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFIsBigEndian
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the file is big-endian.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFIsBigTIFF
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the file is a BigTIFF (64-bit offsets).
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFGetReadProc
functions.description: Returns the client read callback for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFGetWriteProc
functions.description: Returns the client write callback for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFGetSeekProc
functions.description: Returns the client seek callback for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFGetCloseProc
functions.description: Returns the client close callback for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFGetSizeProc
functions.description: Returns the client size callback for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFGetMapFileProc
functions.description: Returns the client map-file callback for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFGetUnmapFileProc
functions.description: Returns the client unmap-file callback for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFCurrentRow
functions.description: Returns the current row being processed for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFCurrentDirectory
functions.description: Returns the index of the current directory (IFD).
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFNumberOfDirectories
functions.description: Returns the number of directories (IFDs) in the file.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFCurrentDirOffset
functions.description: Returns the file offset of the current directory (IFD).
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFCurrentStrip
functions.description: Returns the current strip index.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFCurrentTile
functions.description: Returns the current tile index.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFReadBufferSetup
functions.description: Sets up the read buffer for the TIFF handle, optionally with user-provided memory.
requirements: tif must be valid.
If bp is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least size bytes that remains valid during reads.
size must be >= 0.

functions.name: TIFFWriteBufferSetup
functions.description: Sets up the write buffer for the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.
If bp is non-NULL, it must point to a buffer of at least size bytes that remains valid during writes.
size must be >= 0.

functions.name: TIFFSetupStrips
functions.description: Initializes internal strip-related structures for the current image.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Image must have required tags for strips set.

functions.name: TIFFWriteCheck
functions.description: Checks whether writing is possible given current state and optional module name.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Second argument is an int flag (semantics library-defined).
Module string may be NULL or a valid C string.

functions.name: TIFFFreeDirectory
functions.description: Frees the internal directory structures of the TIFF handle.
requirements: tif must be valid.
After freeing, directory contents are invalid until recreated.

functions.name: TIFFCreateDirectory
functions.description: Creates a new directory (IFD) in memory for subsequent writing.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Call before setting tags for a new IFD.

functions.name: TIFFCreateCustomDirectory
functions.description: Creates a new directory using a custom field array definition.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Field array must describe custom tags used.

functions.name: TIFFCreateEXIFDirectory
functions.description: Creates a new EXIF IFD in memory.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFCreateGPSDirectory
functions.description: Creates a new GPS IFD in memory.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFLastDirectory
functions.description: Returns nonzero if the current directory is the last one in the file.
requirements: tif must be valid.

functions.name: TIFFSetDirectory
functions.description: Sets the current directory by index.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Directory index must be within [0, TIFFNumberOfDirectories(tif)-1].
Returns nonzero on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: TIFFSetSubDirectory
functions.description: Sets the current directory by file offset of an IFD.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Offset must point to a valid IFD.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFUnlinkDirectory
functions.description: Removes a directory from the file by index.
requirements: tif must be valid and opened for update.
Index must be valid.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFSetField
functions.description: Sets a tag’s value(s) via varargs.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Arguments must match the tag’s expected types and counts.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: TIFFVSetField
functions.description: va_list variant of TIFFSetField.
requirements: tif must be valid.
va_list must contain arguments matching the tag’s expected types.
Returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.

functions.name: TIFFUnsetField
functions.description: Unsets a tag value in the current directory.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Tag must be set or recognized.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFWriteDirectory
functions.description: Writes the current in-memory directory to the file and prepares for a new one.
requirements: tif must be valid and opened for writing.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFWriteCustomDirectory
functions.description: Writes the current custom directory and returns its offset.
requirements: tif must be valid and opened for writing.
Output offset pointer must be non-NULL.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFCheckpointDirectory
functions.description: Writes partial directory information to ensure recoverability (checkpoint).
requirements: tif must be valid and opened for writing.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFRewriteDirectory
functions.description: Rewrites the current directory in-place if possible.
requirements: tif must be valid and opened for update.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFDeferStrileArrayWriting
functions.description: Defers writing of strip/tile offset/bytecount arrays to directory write-time.
requirements: tif must be valid.
Call before writing image data that would set strile arrays.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFForceStrileArrayWriting
functions.description: Forces immediate writing of strip/tile offset/bytecount arrays.
requirements: tif must be valid and opened for writing.
Returns nonzero on success.

functions.name: TIFFPrintDirectory
functions.description: Prints a human-readable representation of the current directory to a FILE* with optional flags.
requirements: tif must be valid.
FILE* must be a valid output stream.
Flags is a bit-or of TIFFPRINT_* constants.

functions.name: TIFFReadScanline
functions.signature: int TIFFReadScanline(TIFF *tif, void *buf, uint32_t row, uint16_t sample);
functions.description: Reads one scanline of image data into buf.
requirements: tif must be valid and in a readable state.
buf must point to at least TIFFScanlineSize(tif) bytes.
row must be within image height.
For separate samples, sample selects the plane.
Returns 1 on success, -1/0 on error (library-defined).

functions.name: TIFFWriteScanline

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for null-terminated C strings suitable for libtiff APIs expecting
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and filename-like inputs.
# We craft a corpus of interesting, valid strings including:
# - Non-empty ASCII words (for codec names, tag names)
# - Filenames and mode strings
# - Strings with spaces, punctuation, long lengths
# - Embedded printable control-like escapes but still valid as C strings
# All strings are NUL-terminated in the final byte stream.

_MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(0, len(items))]

def _make_ascii_word(rng: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=32) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

def _make_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    exts = [".tif", ".tiff", ".TIF", ".TIFF", ".bin", ".dat"]
    prefixes = ["/tmp/", "./", "../", "C:/temp/", "D:/", ""]
    stem = _make_ascii_word(rng, 1, 16)
    # Occasionally include dots/spaces in stem to exercise edge paths
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        stem = stem + (" " if rng.random() < 0.5 else ".") + _make_ascii_word(rng, 1, 6)
    return _rand_choice(rng, prefixes) + stem + _rand_choice(rng, exts)

def _make_tag_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common tag-like names; TIFFMergeFieldInfo requires non-empty names
    base = _rand_choice(rng, [
        "Software", "Artist", "Make", "Model", "Copyright",
        "PageName", "DocumentName", "HostComputer", "DateTime",
        "ImageDescription", "Compression", "Photometric",
        "TileWidth", "TileLength", "StripOffsets", "StripByteCounts"
    ])
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        base += "_" + _make_ascii_word(rng, 2, 8)
    return base

def _make_codec_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Likely codec names
    names = [
        "LZW", "PackBits", "Deflate", "ZIP", "CCITT_RLE",
        "JPEG", "JBIG", "LERC", "ZSTD", "WEBP", "LZMA",
    ]
    name = _rand_choice(rng, names)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        name += "-" + _make_ascii_word(rng, 2, 6)
    return name

def _make_mode(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return _rand_choice(rng, ["r", "w", "r+", "w+", "a", "a+"])

def _make_message(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = [
        _rand_choice(rng, ["info", "warn", "error", "debug", "codec", "tiff"]),
        _make_ascii_word(rng, 3, 10),
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(str(rng.randint(0, 9999)))
    # include some punctuation
    punct = _rand_choice(rng, [":", ",", ".", " - ", " | "])
    return punct.join(parts)

def _ntbs(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Ensure no embedded NULs; these are intended as C strings
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore') + b"\x00"

def _build_strings_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus: List[bytes] = []
    # Essential entries used by stubs
    corpus.append(_ntbs("fuzz"))                 # generic non-empty
    corpus.append(_ntbs("fuzz.tif"))             # filename fallback
    corpus.append(_ntbs("warn"))
    corpus.append(_ntbs("err"))
    corpus.append(_ntbs("fuzz_tag"))
    # Codec names
    for _ in range(6):
        corpus.append(_ntbs(_make_codec_name(rng)))
    # Filenames
    for _ in range(6):
        corpus.append(_ntbs(_make_filename(rng)))
    # Tag-like names
    for _ in range(6):
        corpus.append(_ntbs(_make_tag_name(rng)))
    # Messages
    for _ in range(6):
        corpus.append(_ntbs(_make_message(rng)))
    # Modes
    for _ in range(3):
        corpus.append(_ntbs(_make_mode(rng)))
    # Longer strings to exercise internal copies
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        long_s = _make_ascii_word(rng, 64, 256)
        corpus.append(_ntbs(long_s))
    # Strings with spaces and punctuation
    for _ in range(4):
        s = _make_ascii_word(rng, 3, 10) + " " + _make_ascii_word(rng, 3, 10)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            s += _rand_choice(rng, [".", ",", ":", ";"])
        corpus.append(_ntbs(s))
    return corpus

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build a sequence of null-terminated strings that the fuzz harness will
    # consume via FUZZ_PARAM_STR(). The harness may request many strings across
    # different stubs; we provide a diverse but valid set. No filenames need to
    # point to real files since these stubs don't open them.
    corpus = _build_strings_corpus(rng)

    # Shuffle to vary ordering between seeds and calls
    rng.shuffle(corpus)

    # Optionally duplicate some entries to increase chance of common cases
    extras: List[bytes] = []
    for b in corpus[: min(5, len(corpus))]:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            extras.append(b)
    corpus.extend(extras)

    # Concatenate into a single buffer, bounded by 4096 bytes
    out = bytearray()
    for s in corpus:
        if len(out) + len(s) > _MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out.extend(s)

    return bytes(out)

# Generator for filesystem path inputs that will be mapped to a filename
# containing a valid TIFF file. The fuzz stubs open the returned filename
# with modes r/r+/w/w+. We provide a readable regular TIFF so that both
# TIFFOpen and TIFFOpenExt succeed for r/r+ and w/w+ (opening an existing
# file in update). The harness maps the returned bytes to a file; we thus
# emit a small, valid Classic TIFF with one minimal IFD and 1x1 pixel
# uncompressed image data. We then place the filename as the first bytes,
# followed by the file content. The typical harness will write the content
# at that path; if it only needs the path, it will still find a valid file
# payload adjacent per its conventions. We keep under 4096 bytes.

# Minimal Classic TIFF (little-endian) with 1x1, 8-bit, 1-sample, Photometric=BlackIsZero,
# one strip with one byte of data (value 0). Required tags: 256(ImageWidth),257(ImageLength),
# 258(BitsPerSample),259(Compression=1),262(Photometric=1),273(StripOffsets),277(SamplesPerPixel=1),
# 278(RowsPerStrip=1),279(StripByteCounts=1),284(PlanarConfig=1).

# TIFF constants
TIFF_LITTLE_ENDIAN_MAGIC = 0x4949  # 'II'
TIFF_VERSION_CLASSIC = 42

# Helper to build a simple Classic TIFF in little endian

def build_minimal_classic_tiff(pixel_value: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # Offsets are from start of file. We will layout:
    # 0x00: 2 bytes 'II'
    # 0x02: 2 bytes version 42
    # 0x04: 4 bytes offset to IFD (we place IFD right after header)
    # Then IFD with N entries and nextIFD=0
    # Data area for: BitsPerSample (SHORT), StripOffsets if we choose to place data after IFD, pixel data
    # We'll place pixel data at the very end as 1 byte.

    # Header size 8 bytes
    header_size = 8

    # We will craft IFD with 10 entries
    entries = []

    # We will determine offsets after knowing IFD size.
    num_entries = 10
    ifd_entry_size = 12
    ifd_size = 2 + num_entries * ifd_entry_size + 4  # count + entries + nextIFD
    ifd_offset = header_size  # place IFD immediately after header

    # Data area will follow IFD
    data_offset_base = ifd_offset + ifd_size

    # Place BitsPerSample (SHORT, count=1) directly in value field (2 bytes), since fits.
    bits_per_sample = 8

    # Pixel data: 1 byte, set StripOffsets to its offset
    pixel_data_offset = data_offset_base
    pixel_data = bytes([pixel_value & 0xFF])

    # No other out-of-line data; all other fit in value fields

    # Build entries helper
    def pack_entry(tag, typ, count, value_bytes):
        # Ensure value_bytes length <= 4; pad with zeros little-endian
        vb = value_bytes.ljust(4, b"\x00")
        return struct.pack('<HHI4s', tag, typ, count, vb)

    def val_u16(v):
        return struct.pack('<H', v)

    def val_u32(v):
        return struct.pack('<I', v)

    # Tag 256 ImageWidth: LONG (4), count=1, value=1
    entries.append(pack_entry(256, 4, 1, val_u32(1)))
    # Tag 257 ImageLength: LONG, 1
    entries.append(pack_entry(257, 4, 1, val_u32(1)))
    # Tag 258 BitsPerSample: SHORT (3), count=1, value=8 (fits in 4 bytes)
    entries.append(pack_entry(258, 3, 1, val_u16(bits_per_sample)))
    # Tag 259 Compression: SHORT, 1 (no compression)
    entries.append(pack_entry(259, 3, 1, val_u16(1)))
    # Tag 262 PhotometricInterpretation: SHORT, 1 (BlackIsZero)
    entries.append(pack_entry(262, 3, 1, val_u16(1)))
    # Tag 273 StripOffsets: LONG, 1, value=pixel_data_offset
    entries.append(pack_entry(273, 4, 1, val_u32(pixel_data_offset)))
    # Tag 277 SamplesPerPixel: SHORT, 1
    entries.append(pack_entry(277, 3, 1, val_u16(1)))
    # Tag 278 RowsPerStrip: LONG, 1 = 1
    entries.append(pack_entry(278, 4, 1, val_u32(1)))
    # Tag 279 StripByteCounts: LONG, 1 = 1
    entries.append(pack_entry(279, 4, 1, val_u32(1)))
    # Tag 284 PlanarConfiguration: SHORT, 1 = 1 (contig)
    entries.append(pack_entry(284, 3, 1, val_u16(1)))

    # Assemble file
    parts = []
    # Header
    parts.append(struct.pack('<HHI', TIFF_LITTLE_ENDIAN_MAGIC, TIFF_VERSION_CLASSIC, ifd_offset))
    # IFD count
    parts.append(struct.pack('<H', num_entries))
    # Entries (already in little-endian with packed fields)
    parts.extend(entries)
    # nextIFD = 0
    parts.append(struct.pack('<I', 0))
    # Data area: pixel byte
    parts.append(pixel_data)

    blob = b''.join(parts)
    return blob


def _random_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a short, portable relative path, optionally with subdir-like components.
    # Avoid characters that may be unsupported. Keep within 64 chars.
    components = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 2)
    for _ in range(depth):
        n = rng.randint(1, 8)
        name = ''.join(rng.choices(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '_-.', k=n))

    base_choices = [
        'test', 'image', 'sample', 'tiny', 'tile', 'strip', 'rgba', 'classic', 'bigtiffhint'

    variant = ''.join(rng.choices(string.digits, k=rng.randint(0, 3)))
    fname = base + variant + '.tif'
    components.append(fname)
    path = '/'.join(components)
    return path


def build_bundle(path: str, content: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Bundle the filename and the file contents in a single buffer.
    # Layout:
    # [u16 path_len][path bytes UTF-8][file bytes]
    # This is a common pattern for fuzz harnesses that need both.
    p = path.encode('utf-8')
    if len(p) > 1024:
        p = p[:1024]
    return struct.pack('<H', len(p)) + p + content

        entries.append(be_pack_entry(257, 4, 1, struct.pack('>I', 1)))
        entries.append(be_pack_entry(258, 3, 1, struct.pack('>H', 8)))
        entries.append(be_pack_entry(259, 3, 1, struct.pack('>H', 1)))
        entries.append(be_pack_entry(262, 3, 1, struct.pack('>H', 1)))
        entries.append(be_pack_entry(273, 4, 1, struct.pack('>I', pixel_off)))
        entries.append(be_pack_entry(277, 3, 1, struct.pack('>H', 1)))
        entries.append(be_pack_entry(278, 4, 1, struct.pack('>I', 1)))

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generates minimal but valid Classic TIFF and BigTIFF files with small images.
# We try to cover:
# - Little and big endian
# - ClassicTIFF (version 42) and BigTIFF (version 43)
# - Strips vs tiles (minimal 1x1 tile or single strip)
# - Photometric: RGB, Gray, Palette
# - BitsPerSample: 8, 16
# - Compression: None (1) for simplicity and validity
# - PlanarConfiguration: Contig (1)
# The generated file should open with TIFFOpen(r/r+). For w/w+, random content may still be OK
# since libtiff opens and may create/overwrite, but we focus on readable formats.

# Helpers for endian-aware packing

def pack_u16(val: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H" if be else "<H", val & 0xFFFF)

def pack_s16(val: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">h" if be else "<h", val)

def pack_u32(val: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I" if be else "<I", val & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def pack_u64(val: int, be: bool) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">Q" if be else "<Q", val & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)

# TIFF tag constants
TAG_ImageWidth = 256
TAG_ImageLength = 257
TAG_BitsPerSample = 258
TAG_Compression = 259
TAG_Photometric = 262
TAG_StripOffsets = 273
TAG_SamplesPerPixel = 277
TAG_RowsPerStrip = 278
TAG_StripByteCounts = 279
TAG_PlanarConfiguration = 284
TAG_TileWidth = 322
TAG_TileLength = 323
TAG_TileOffsets = 324
TAG_TileByteCounts = 325
TAG_ColorMap = 320

# TIFF data types
TYPE_BYTE = 1
TYPE_ASCII = 2
TYPE_SHORT = 3
TYPE_LONG = 4
TYPE_RATIONAL = 5
TYPE_SBYTE = 6
TYPE_UNDEFINED = 7
TYPE_SSHORT = 8
TYPE_SLONG = 9
TYPE_SRATIONAL = 10
TYPE_FLOAT = 11
TYPE_DOUBLE = 12
TYPE_IFD = 13
# BigTIFF uses 64-bit counts/offsets and types LONG8/SLONG8/IFD8 but the IFD value field remains 8 bytes

# Compression constants
COMP_NONE = 1

# Photometric
PHOTO_MINISBLACK = 1
PHOTO_RGB = 2
PHOTO_PALETTE = 3

# PlanarConfiguration
PLANAR_CONTIG = 1


def align(pos: int, n: int) -> int:
    r = pos % n
    return pos if r == 0 else (pos + (n - r))


def make_classic_ifd(entries: List[Tuple[int, int, int, bytes]], be: bool, next_ifd: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # Classic TIFF IFD layout: count(2), entries, next_ifd_offset(4)
    # Each entry: tag(2), type(2), count(4), value_or_offset(4)
    # For VALUEs whose total size <=4, inline; else append data and point to it.
    out = io.BytesIO()
    # Placeholder for count
    out.write(pack_u16(len(entries), be))
    # We'll temporarily write entries with value_or_offset=0, then patch
    entry_pos_list = []
    data_area = io.BytesIO()
    # Current absolute base offset (caller must place IFD at known offset and then add data after it).
    # We will assume the IFD starts at some offset; caller computes and patches offsets relative to file start.
    # To keep it simple, we first build with relative positions assuming IFD at offset 0, and the caller will
    # adjust by adding the real IFD start offset when writing final file.
    cur_ifd_data_offset = 2 + len(entries) * 12 + 4  # after entries and next_ifd

    for tag, typ, count, raw in entries:
        # Compute size per type
        type_size = {TYPE_BYTE:1, TYPE_ASCII:1, TYPE_SHORT:2, TYPE_LONG:4, TYPE_RATIONAL:8,
                     TYPE_SBYTE:1, TYPE_UNDEFINED:1, TYPE_SSHORT:2, TYPE_SLONG:4, TYPE_SRATIONAL:8,
                     TYPE_FLOAT:4, TYPE_DOUBLE:8, TYPE_IFD:4}.get(typ, 1)
        total = type_size * count
        out.write(pack_u16(tag, be))
        out.write(pack_u16(typ, be))
        out.write(pack_u32(count, be))
        if total <= 4:
            # Inline value (pad to 4)
            v = raw.ljust(4, b"\x00")
            out.write(v)
        else:
            # Needs offset; record position and append to data_area
            entry_value_pos = out.tell()
            out.write(pack_u32(0, be))  # placeholder
            # align data_area to type_size for good measure
            pad_to = type_size if type_size in (2, 4, 8) else 1
            data_area.seek(align(data_area.tell(), pad_to))
            data_offset = cur_ifd_data_offset + align(data_area.tell(), 1)
            # write data
            data_area.write(raw)
            entry_pos_list.append((entry_value_pos, data_offset))
    # next IFD offset
    out.write(pack_u32(next_ifd, be))
    # Now append data area and patch offsets
    base = out.getvalue()
    buf = bytearray(base)
    for pos, offs in entry_pos_list:
        # offs is relative to start of IFD=0; caller must add real ifd_start later.
        # Here we keep as-is; caller will fix by adding the actual IFD start.
        struct.pack_into((">I" if be else "<I"), buf, pos, offs)
    return bytes(buf) + data_area.getvalue()


def fix_classic_ifd_offsets(buf: bytearray, ifd_start: int, be: bool) -> None:

        type_size = {TYPE_BYTE:1, TYPE_ASCII:1, TYPE_SHORT:2, TYPE_LONG:4, TYPE_RATIONAL:8,
                     TYPE_SBYTE:1, TYPE_UNDEFINED:1, TYPE_SSHORT:2, TYPE_SLONG:4, TYPE_SRATIONAL:8,
                     TYPE_FLOAT:4, TYPE_DOUBLE:8, TYPE_IFD:4}.get(typ, 1)
        total = type_size * cnt
        if total > 4:
            off = struct.unpack(">I" if be else "<I", buf[pos+8:pos+12])[0]
            off += ifd_start
            struct.pack_into(">I" if be else "<I", buf, pos+8, off)
        pos += 12
    # next IFD offset remains unchanged (we wrote absolute file offset outside)


def build_classic_tiff(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    be = rnd.choice([False, True])
    # Minimal small image sizes
    width = rnd.choice([1, 2, 3, 8, 16])
    height = rnd.choice([1, 2, 3, 8, 16])
    bits_per_sample = rnd.choice([8, 16])
    photometric = rnd.choice([PHOTO_MINISBLACK, PHOTO_RGB, PHOTO_PALETTE])
    compression = COMP_NONE
    planar = PLANAR_CONTIG

    # For simplicity, choose strips, 1 strip for whole image
    samples_per_pixel = 1
    if photometric == PHOTO_RGB:
        samples_per_pixel = 3
    elif photometric == PHOTO_PALETTE:
        samples_per_pixel = 1

    # Compute bytes per sample
    bps = bits_per_sample
    bytes_per_sample = 1 if bps == 8 else 2
    # Row size in bytes for contig
    rowbytes = width * samples_per_pixel * bytes_per_sample
    image_bytes = rowbytes * height

    # Build image data (simple gradient/pattern) within file
    def make_image_data() -> bytes:
        if bits_per_sample == 8:
            # Simple pattern
            data = bytearray(image_bytes)
            for y in range(height):
                for x in range(width):
                    if photometric == PHOTO_RGB:
                        r = (x * 31 + y * 17) & 0xFF
                        g = (x * 13 + y * 29) & 0xFF
                        b = (x * 7 + y * 3) & 0xFF
                        idx = y * rowbytes + x * 3
                        data[idx] = r
                        data[idx+1] = g
                        data[idx+2] = b
                    else:
                        v = (x * 17 + y * 13) & 0xFF
                        idx = y * rowbytes + x
                        data[idx] = v
            return bytes(data)
        else:
            # 16-bit: scale 0..65535 patterns, little/big endian does not matter for raw data validity
            data = bytearray(image_bytes)
            for y in range(height):
                for x in range(width):
                    if photometric == PHOTO_RGB:
                        r = ((x * 257) ^ (y * 521)) & 0xFFFF
                        g = ((x * 123) ^ (y * 911)) & 0xFFFF
                        b = ((x * 777) ^ (y * 369)) & 0xFFFF
                        base = y * rowbytes + x * 6
                        struct.pack_into(">H" if be else "<H", data, base, r)
                        struct.pack_into(">H" if be else "<H", data, base+2, g)
                        struct.pack_into(">H" if be else "<H", data, base+4, b)
                    else:
                        v = ((x * 1453 + y * 827) & 0xFFFF)
                        base = y * rowbytes + x * 2
                        struct.pack_into(">H" if be else "<H", data, base, v)
            return bytes(data)

    img = make_image_data()

    # Optional palette for PHOTO_PALETTE: 256 or 2^bits entries. Use 256 entries of 16-bit per channel (R,G,B arrays)
    palette_entries = 1 << min(bits_per_sample, 8)
    colormap_data = b""
    if photometric == PHOTO_PALETTE:
        # Build simple grayscale palette
        reds = bytearray()
        greens = bytearray()
        blues = bytearray()
        for i in range(palette_entries):
            val = int(i * 65535 // (palette_entries - 1 if palette_entries > 1 else 1))
            reds += pack_u16(val, be)
            greens += pack_u16(val, be)
            blues += pack_u16(val, be)
        colormap_data = bytes(reds + greens + blues)

    # Build IFD entries list: (tag, type, count, rawbytes)
    entries: List[Tuple[int, int, int, bytes]] = []
    # ImageWidth, ImageLength
    entries.append((TAG_ImageWidth, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(width, be)))
    entries.append((TAG_ImageLength, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(height, be)))
    # BitsPerSample: for RGB, 3 SHORTs; else 1 SHORT
    if samples_per_pixel == 3:
        bps_arr = pack_u16(bits_per_sample, be) * 3
        entries.append((TAG_BitsPerSample, TYPE_SHORT, 3, bps_arr))
    else:
        entries.append((TAG_BitsPerSample, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(bits_per_sample, be)))
    # Compression
    entries.append((TAG_Compression, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(compression, be)))
    # Photometric
    entries.append((TAG_Photometric, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(photometric, be)))
    # SamplesPerPixel
    entries.append((TAG_SamplesPerPixel, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(samples_per_pixel, be)))
    # PlanarConfiguration
    entries.append((TAG_PlanarConfiguration, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(PLANAR_CONTIG, be)))
    # Strips setup: one strip
    rows_per_strip = height
    entries.append((TAG_RowsPerStrip, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(rows_per_strip, be)))
    # StripByteCounts: one LONG
    entries.append((TAG_StripByteCounts, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(image_bytes, be)))
    # StripOffsets: one LONG -> will point to image data
    # Placeholder raw; actual offset filled by builder then patched
    entries.append((TAG_StripOffsets, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(0, be)))
    # ColorMap if paletted
    if photometric == PHOTO_PALETTE:
        entries.append((TAG_ColorMap, TYPE_SHORT, palette_entries * 3, colormap_data))

    # Build classic header
    # Header: byte order, 42, IFD offset (4)
    header = io.BytesIO()
    header.write(b"MM" if be else b"II")
    header.write(pack_u16(42, be))
    # We'll place IFD right after header (8 bytes), but if inline data grows, it's okay; entries with large data have offsets patched.
    ifd_offset = 8
    header.write(pack_u32(ifd_offset, be))

    # Build IFD block with relative offsets; we'll later fix to file absolute
    ifd_block = make_classic_ifd(entries, be, next_ifd=0)

    # We need to know where StripOffsets data is stored (for inline <=4 it is inline). For StripOffsets (one LONG), total size=4 -> inline.
    # In our entries, StripOffsets is inline 4 bytes inside the IFD entry. We'll patch it to absolute image data offset later.

    # Assemble file: header + IFD + data blobs (from make_classic_ifd) + image data
    filebuf = bytearray()
    filebuf += header.getvalue()
    ifd_start = len(filebuf)
    filebuf += ifd_block

    # Patch offsets inside IFD entries that pointed to extra data (BitsPerSample for RGB, ColorMap)
    fix_classic_ifd_offsets(filebuf, ifd_start, be)

    # Compute image data offset aligned to 4 bytes
    img_off = align(len(filebuf), 4)
    if img_off > len(filebuf):
        filebuf += b"\x00" * (img_off - len(filebuf))
    # Append image data
    filebuf += img

    # Now patch StripOffsets entry inline value to img_off
    # Find entry list and locate tag 273
    count = struct.unpack(">H" if be else "<H", filebuf[ifd_start:ifd_start+2])[0]
    pos = ifd_start + 2
    for _ in range(count):
        tag = struct.unpack(">H" if be else "<H", filebuf[pos:pos+2])[0]
        typ = struct.unpack(">H" if be else "<H", filebuf[pos+2:pos+4])[0]
        cnt = struct.unpack(">I" if be else "<I", filebuf[pos+4:pos+8])[0]
        if tag == TAG_StripOffsets and typ == TYPE_LONG and cnt == 1:
            struct.pack_into(">I" if be else "<I", filebuf, pos+8, img_off)
            break
        pos += 12

    return bytes(filebuf)


def build_bigtiff(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A5_5A5A)
    be = rnd.choice([False, True])
    width = rnd.choice([1, 2, 4, 8])
    height = rnd.choice([1, 2, 4, 8])
    bits_per_sample = rnd.choice([8, 16])
    photometric = rnd.choice([PHOTO_MINISBLACK, PHOTO_RGB])  # keep simpler for BigTIFF
    compression = COMP_NONE
    samples_per_pixel = 3 if photometric == PHOTO_RGB else 1
    bytes_per_sample = 1 if bits_per_sample == 8 else 2
    rowbytes = width * samples_per_pixel * bytes_per_sample
    image_bytes = rowbytes * height

    # Build raw image data
    data = bytearray(image_bytes)
    for y in range(height):
        for x in range(width):
            if samples_per_pixel == 3:
                r = (x * 31 + y * 17) & 0xFF
                g = (x * 13 + y * 29) & 0xFF
                b = (x * 7 + y * 3) & 0xFF
                if bits_per_sample == 8:
                    base = y * rowbytes + x * 3
                    data[base] = r
                    data[base+1] = g
                    data[base+2] = b
                else:
                    base = y * rowbytes + x * 6
                    struct.pack_into(">H" if be else "<H", data, base, r * 257)
                    struct.pack_into(">H" if be else "<H", data, base+2, g * 257)
                    struct.pack_into(">H" if be else "<H", data, base+4, b * 257)
            else:
                v = (x * 17 + y * 13) & 0xFF
                if bits_per_sample == 8:
                    data[y * rowbytes + x] = v
                else:
                    struct.pack_into(">H" if be else "<H", data, y * rowbytes + x * 2, v * 257)
    img = bytes(data)

    # BigTIFF header: byte order, 43, offsetsize=8, unused=0, first_ifd_offset (8)
    header = io.BytesIO()
    header.write(b"MM" if be else b"II")
    header.write(pack_u16(43, be))
    header.write(pack_u16(8, be))  # offset size
    header.write(pack_u16(0, be))  # unused
    first_ifd_off = 16  # immediately after header
    header.write(pack_u64(first_ifd_off, be))

    # BigTIFF IFD layout: count(8), entries, next_ifd_offset(8)
    # Entry: tag(2), type(2), count(8), value_or_offset(8)
    entries: List[Tuple[int, int, int, bytes]] = []

    # Prepare tag raw data
    def raw_short_array(vals: List[int]) -> bytes:
        b = io.BytesIO()
        for v in vals:
            b.write(pack_u16(v, be))
        return b.getvalue()

    entries.append((TAG_ImageWidth, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(width, be)))
    entries.append((TAG_ImageLength, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(height, be)))
    if samples_per_pixel == 3:
        entries.append((TAG_BitsPerSample, TYPE_SHORT, 3, raw_short_array([bits_per_sample]*3)))
    else:
        entries.append((TAG_BitsPerSample, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(bits_per_sample, be)))
    entries.append((TAG_Compression, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(compression, be)))
    entries.append((TAG_Photometric, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(photometric, be)))
    entries.append((TAG_SamplesPerPixel, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(samples_per_pixel, be)))
    entries.append((TAG_PlanarConfiguration, TYPE_SHORT, 1, pack_u16(PLANAR_CONTIG, be)))
    entries.append((TAG_RowsPerStrip, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(height, be)))
    entries.append((TAG_StripByteCounts, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u32(image_bytes, be)))
    # StripOffsets (one LONG8 in BigTIFF is typically type IFD8=18 but using LONG with 1 value fits in 8-byte field too).
    # We'll write as LONG with 1 count; store 8-byte field value
    entries.append((TAG_StripOffsets, TYPE_LONG, 1, pack_u64(0, be)))

    # Build IFD with external data area
    ifd = io.BytesIO()
    ifd.write(pack_u64(len(entries), be))
    # We'll record entries needing external storage (BitsPerSample for RGB)
    fixups = []  # list of (value_pos_in_ifd, absolute_offset)
    data_area = io.BytesIO()

    def write_entry(tag: int, typ: int, count: int, raw: bytes):
        ifd.write(pack_u16(tag, be))
        ifd.write(pack_u16(typ, be))
        ifd.write(pack_u64(count, be))
        # size per type
        type_size = {TYPE_BYTE:1, TYPE_ASCII:1, TYPE_SHORT:2, TYPE_LONG:4, TYPE_RATIONAL:8,
                     TYPE_SBYTE:1, TYPE_UNDEFINED:1, TYPE_SSHORT:2, TYPE_SLONG:4, TYPE_SRATIONAL:8,
                     TYPE_FLOAT:4, TYPE_DOUBLE:8, TYPE_IFD:8}.get(typ, 1)
        total = type_size * count
        if total <= 8:
            v = raw.ljust(8, b"\x00")
            ifd.write(v)
        else:
            # store in data area, aligned
            pad_to = 8 if type_size >= 8 else (4 if type_size >= 4 else (2 if type_size >= 2 else 1))
            data_area.seek(align(data_area.tell(), pad_to))
            value_off = 16 + 8 + len(entries)*20 + 8 + data_area.tell()  # header(16) + count(8) + entries(20 each) + next(8) + data_off
            ifd.write(pack_u64(value_off, be))
            data_area.write(raw)

    for tag, typ, cnt, raw in entries:
        write_entry(tag, typ, cnt, raw)

    # next IFD offset = 0
    ifd.write(pack_u64(0, be))

    # Assemble file
    filebuf = bytearray()
    filebuf += header.getvalue()
    filebuf += ifd.getvalue()
    # Align to 8 before data area as we used 8-byte alignment
    data_start = align(len(filebuf), 8)
    if data_start > len(filebuf):
        filebuf += b"\x00" * (data_start - len(filebuf))
    filebuf += data_area.getvalue()

    # Append image data aligned to 8 and patch StripOffsets entry inline value (8 bytes field)
    img_off = align(len(filebuf), 8)
    if img_off > len(filebuf):
        filebuf += b"\x00" * (img_off - len(filebuf))
    filebuf += img

    # Locate StripOffsets entry and patch 8-byte value
    # IFD starts at offset 16; iterate entries
    ifd_start = 16
    nent = struct.unpack(">Q" if be else "<Q", filebuf[ifd_start:ifd_start+8])[0]
    pos = ifd_start + 8
    for _ in range(nent):
        tag = struct.unpack(">H" if be else "<H", filebuf[pos:pos+2])[0]
        typ = struct.unpack(">H" if be else "<H", filebuf[pos+2:pos+4])[0]
        cnt = struct.unpack(">Q" if be else "<Q", filebuf[pos+4:pos+12])[0]
        if tag == TAG_StripOffsets and cnt == 1:
            struct.pack_into(">Q" if be else "<Q", filebuf, pos+12, img_off)
            break
        pos += 20

    return bytes(filebuf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Prefer generating readable TIFFs for the fuzzer stub that opens files.
    choice = rnd.random()
    if choice < 0.6:
        data = build_classic_tiff(seed)
    else:
        data = build_bigtiff(seed)
    # Ensure size limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # Downscale by regenerating with smaller dims deterministically
        data = build_classic_tiff(seed & 0xFFFF)
        if len(data) > 4096:
            data = data[:4096]
    return data
